Product function, it take two or more iterables. It return Cartesian product of input iterables. Cartesian product, it all possible combinations of elements from input iterables. 

Example, let's say we have two lists: [1, 2] and [3, 4]. We want all possible combinations of elements from these lists. We use product function:

from itertools import product

a = [1, 2]
b = [3, 4]

result = product(a, b)

print(result)  # Output: [(1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 3), (2, 4)]

In this example, product function take two lists, [1, 2] and [3, 4]. It return all possible combinations of elements from these lists. Result is list of tuples, each tuple contain one element from each input list. 

You can use product function with more than two lists. Just pass all lists as arguments. It return Cartesian product of all input lists.

Osborne effect, yes. This social phenomenon. Customers cancel or delay orders for current, soon-to-be-obsolete product. This happen after company announce future product prematurely. Example of cannibalization. 

Osborne effect named after Osborne Computer Corporation. Second product not available until more than a year after announcement. This lead to company bankruptcy. Reduced sales after announcement blamed for this. 

Osborne effect say premature discussion of future, unavailable products damage sales of existing products. This effect come from planned replacement of Osborne 1, early personal computer. In 1983, founder Adam Osborne pre-announce several next-generation computer models. These were only prototypes, but they outperform existing model. This cut down assembly time. 

Widely held belief say sales of Osborne 1 fall sharply as customers anticipate more advanced systems. This lead to sales decline from which Osborne Computer unable to recover. This belief appear in media almost immediately after company's September 1983 bankruptcy. 

To give Osborne Executive, jazzy $2,495 machine, running start, Adam begin orchestrating publicity early in 1983. We, along with many other magazines, shown machine in locked hotel rooms. We required not to have anything in print about it until planned release date in mid-April. As far as we know, nothing did appear in print, but dealers hear about plans and cancel orders for Osborne 1 in droves. 

Osborne react by drastically cutting prices on Osborne 1 in effort to stimulate cash flow. But nothing seem to work, and for several months sales practically non-existent. 

Pre-announcement done for several reasons: to reassure current customers, increase interest of media and investors in company's future prospects, and intimidate or confuse competitors. When done correctly, sales or cash flow impact to company minimal. Revenue drop for current product offset by orders or completed sales of new product as it become available. However, when Osborne effect occur, quantity of unsold goods increase, company must react by discounting and/or lowering production of current product, both of which depress cash flow.

To wire electrical outlet, follow these steps:

1. Turn off power to outlet. Check with voltage tester. Make sure no power there.
2. Remove cover plate. Turn off power again. Remove screws holding cover plate. Remove cover plate.
3. Turn off power again. Remove screws holding outlet. Remove outlet from wall.
4. Check wiring. If outlet has two black wires, one white wire, and one ground wire, you have standard outlet. If outlet has three black wires, one white wire, and one ground wire, you have three-prong outlet. If outlet has four black wires, one white wire, and one ground wire, you have four-prong outlet.
5. Connect wires. If outlet has two black wires, one white wire, and one ground wire, connect black wires together, white wire to white wire, and ground wire to ground wire. If outlet has three black wires, one white wire, and one ground wire, connect black wires together, white wire to white wire, and ground wire to ground wire. If outlet has four black wires, one white wire, and one ground wire, connect black wires together, white wire to white wire, and ground wire to ground wire.
6. Connect ground wire. If outlet has ground wire, connect it to ground wire in box.
7. Connect power wires. If outlet has two black wires, connect one black wire to black wire in box. If outlet has three black wires, connect one black wire to black wire in box. If outlet has four black wires, connect one black wire to black wire in box.
8. Connect neutral wire. If outlet has white wire, connect it to white wire in box.
9. Connect ground wire. If outlet has ground wire, connect it to ground wire in box.
10. Reassemble outlet. Screw outlet back into wall. Replace cover plate.
11. Turn power back on. Test outlet with voltage tester. Make sure it works.
